readings: Match laboratory test records to patients by ID, excluding tests with no matching patient. Group the matched records by the patient's `SEX`, with the empty string as its own group. Compute the average test-record count across all sex groups. For each group whose count exceeds that average, show the sex, its count, its count divided by the total count across all sex groups, and its count minus the average. Do not round any values.

Match laboratory test records to patients by ID, excluding tests with no matching patient. Group the matched records by the patient's `SEX`, with the empty string as its own group. Compute the average test-record count across all sex groups. For each group whose count exceeds that average, show the sex, its count, its count divided by the total count across only the groups that exceed the average, and its count minus the average. Do not round any values.
queries:
WITH sex_counts AS (
    SELECT p.SEX, COUNT(*) AS test_count
    FROM Laboratory AS l
    JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID
    GROUP BY p.SEX
),
totals AS (
    SELECT AVG(test_count) AS avg_count, SUM(test_count) AS total_count
    FROM sex_counts
)
SELECT
    s.SEX,
    s.test_count,
    s.test_count * 1.0 / t.total_count,
    s.test_count - t.avg_count
FROM sex_counts AS s
CROSS JOIN totals AS t
WHERE s.test_count > t.avg_count

WITH sex_counts AS (
    SELECT p.SEX, COUNT(*) AS test_count
    FROM Laboratory AS l
    JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID
    GROUP BY p.SEX
),
above_average AS (
    SELECT SEX, test_count, AVG(test_count) OVER () AS average_count
    FROM sex_counts
)
SELECT
    SEX,
    test_count,
    CAST(test_count AS REAL) / SUM(test_count) OVER () AS proportion,
    test_count - average_count AS difference
FROM above_average
WHERE test_count > average_count
